question: Y92
answer:
Governing document and applicability: NERC PRC-024-3, 'Frequency and Voltage Protection Settings for Generating Resources,' Attachment 2, 'Voltage No-Trip Boundaries – Eastern, Western, and ERCOT Interconnections.' The version history in the standard identifies PRC-024-3 as effective October 1, 2022. Attachment 2 applies a common voltage no-trip boundary table and figure to the Eastern, Western, and ERCOT Interconnections; it does not set different terminal times for those three interconnections.

Answer: The voltage no-trip zone ends at 4 seconds for applicability to PRC-024.

Basis in Attachment 2:

1. Voltage Boundary Data Points, Table 1:
   High Voltage Duration:
   - ≥1.200 pu: 0.00 s
   - ≥1.175 pu: 0.20 s
   - ≥1.15 pu: 0.50 s
   - ≥1.10 pu: 1.00 s
   - <1.10 pu: 4.00 s
   Low Voltage Duration:
   - <0.45 pu: 0.15 s
   - <0.65 pu: 0.30 s
   - <0.75 pu: 2.00 s
   - <0.90 pu: 3.00 s
   - ≥0.90 pu: 4.00 s

2. Figure 1 in Attachment 2 plots Voltage (per unit) against Time (sec), with the time axis running from 0 to 4 seconds. The figure contains the explicit note: 'The Voltage No Trip Zone ends at 4 seconds for applicability to PRC-024.'

3. Both the high-voltage boundary data and the low-voltage boundary data terminate at 4.00 seconds, and the figure's plotted time axis terminates at 4 seconds. Therefore the end of the no-trip zone is not a plot artifact; it is the defined applicability limit of the Attachment 2 voltage no-trip boundary.

Interpretation: For PRC-024-3 Attachment 2, the no-trip region applies up to and including the 4-second boundary. Beyond 4 seconds, Attachment 2 no longer defines a no-trip obligation. The note that the area outside the 'No Trip Zone' is not a 'Must Trip Zone' means that operation outside the boundary does not require tripping; it does not extend the no-trip zone beyond 4 seconds.

Final value: 4 seconds (4.00 s).

question: Y94
answer:
## Bottom line

For 10 CFR Part 431 Subpart K as in force on 2026-11-21: the September 9, 2025 DOE action **removed** the amendments that had been made effective December 23, 2024 (the amendments published at 89 FR 91163, Oct. 9, 2024). The action was taken under the Congressional Review Act pursuant to Pub. L. 119-8, and was published at 90 FR 43371, Sept. 9, 2025. As of Sept. 9, 2025, the affected sections **reverted to the Dec. 22, 2024 version** — i.e., the text as it stood the day before the disapproved amendments took effect.

## Controlling text

The eCFR carries the following editorial note at the head of Part 431 (present on the current pages fetched 2026-11-23, i.e., it is still in force after the 2026-11-21 query date):

> **Editorial Note on Part 431**
> At 90 FR 43371, Sept. 9, 2025, as required by the Congressional Review Act and Pub. L. 119-8, the Department of Energy removed the amendments to several sections in part 431 made effective on Dec. 23, 2024, at 89 FR 91163, Oct. 9, 2024. As of Sept. 9, 2025, the affected sections reverted to the Dec. 22, 2024 version.

That sentence answers both substantive questions directly; nothing below depends on inference from secondary descriptions.

## Document identification

| Element | Identification |
|---|---|
| Instrument | 10 CFR Part 431, Subpart K — Distribution Transformers (§§ 431.191–431.198 and appendix A) |
| Disapproved rule | 89 FR 91163 (Oct. 9, 2024); amendments effective Dec. 23, 2024 |
| Disapproval vehicle | Congressional Review Act, Pub. L. 119-8 (joint resolution of disapproval) |
| Implementing DOE action | 90 FR 43371, Sept. 9, 2025 — removal of the amendments from the CFR text |
| Resulting CFR version | Dec. 22, 2024 version (text in force immediately before the Dec. 23, 2024 effective date) |
| Status on 2026-11-21 | Removal in force; no later Subpart K amendment or stay evidenced |

## Legal mechanism (what the Sept. 9, 2025 action actually did)

1. **It was not a substantive rulemaking.** DOE did not amend standards, issue a technical correction, or withdraw a proposal. It *removed* previously codified text.
2. **The operative legal effect came from the CRA, not from DOE's document.** Under 5 U.S.C. § 801(b)(1) a rule disapproved by joint resolution "shall not take effect (or shall not continue in effect)," and under § 801(f) the disapproved rule is treated as though it had never taken effect. The joint resolution (Pub. L. 119-8) supplies the nullification; 90 FR 43371 is the ministerial Federal Register document by which DOE conformed the CFR text to that nullification.
3. **Reissuance bar.** Under 5 U.S.C. § 801(b)(2), DOE may not reissue the disapproved rule in substantially the same form, nor issue a new rule that implements the same regulatory program, unless subsequently authorized by law. This is why the reverted text — not a re-proposal — is the operative text.
4. **No judicial-review channel.** CRA disapproval is not subject to the ordinary vacatur/stay dynamics of APA litigation (see 5 U.S.C. § 805), so the usual question of "was the rule stayed or vacated before the query date" does not attach to the disapproval itself.

## Section-level effect within Subpart K

Tracing by Federal Register citation in each section's source note (rather than by summary description):

| Section | Citation in current source note | Effect of Sept. 9, 2025 action |
|---|---|---|
| § 431.191 Purpose and scope | [71 FR 24995, Apr. 27, 2006] | Not amended by 89 FR 91163 — unaffected |
| § 431.192 Definitions | [70 FR 60416, Oct. 18, 2005, as amended at 71 FR 24995; 71 FR 60662; 72 FR 58239; 78 FR 23433; 86 FR 51252; 89 FR 30039, Apr. 22, 2024; 90 FR 6795, Jan. 21, 2025] | Amended effective Dec. 23, 2024 by 89 FR 91163; that amendment removed, so definitions reverted to the Dec. 22, 2024 text. Note the 89 FR 91163 citation is absent from the current note — consistent with removal — while the later, independent 90 FR 6795 (Jan. 21, 2025) amendment remains |
| § 431.193 Test procedure | [86 FR 51252, Sept. 14, 2021] | Not amended by 89 FR 91163 — unaffected; still directs to appendix A and limits application to transformers subject to § 431.196 |
| § 431.196 Energy conservation standards and their effective dates | Carries the Part 431 editorial note; tables of standards | Amended effective Dec. 23, 2024 by 89 FR 91163; that amendment removed — section reverted to the Dec. 22, 2024 version (the pre-Oct. 2024 standards regime) |
| Appendix A (test procedure) | [71 FR 24999, Apr. 27, 2006; 71 FR 60662, Oct. 16, 2006; 86 FR 51252, Sept. 14, 2021] | No 89 FR 91163 citation — unaffected; OMB information-collection effective-date note at § 6.2(f) unchanged |

The note's phrase "several sections in part 431" confirms the disapproved rule spanned more than Subpart K; the same removal logic applies to every part 431 section carrying a 89 FR 91163 source citation.

## What "reverted to the Dec. 22, 2024 version" means precisely

It means the affected sections resume the text in force on December 22, 2024 — the last day before the disapproved amendments became effective (Dec. 23, 2024). It does **not** mean a rollback that erases unrelated later amendments. Concretely, in § 431.192 the January 21, 2025 amendment at 90 FR 6795 post-dates the reversion baseline but is not part of the disapproved rule, and it remains in the source note and in the text. Practitioners should therefore read the affected sections as: *Dec. 22, 2024 baseline + any later amendment not traceable to 89 FR 91163*.

## Status as of 2026-11-21

- The editorial note is still displayed on the eCFR "current" pages fetched 2026-11-23, so the removal had not been undone, superseded, or stayed as of the query date.
- No Federal Register citation later than the note itself appears in any Subpart K section source note (the latest is 90 FR 6795, Jan. 21, 2025), so no intervening Subpart K amendment is evidenced between Sept. 9, 2025 and 2026-11-21.
- No court vacatur or stay of the disapproval is possible through ordinary APA channels (§ 805), and none is evidenced.

## Verification items a reviewer should close out (flagged, not resolved here)

1. **Display anomaly in § 431.196.** The current eCFR text of § 431.196 still displays paragraphs keyed to compliance dates of April 23, 2029 (e.g., low-voltage dry-type and submersible transformer tables). That is in tension with the editorial note's "removed." The *legal* answer is unaffected — a CRA disapproval renders the rule of no effect as a matter of law, and DOE has stated the sections reverted — but the residual table text should be confirmed against the Federal Register document at 90 FR 43371 and the eCFR change history for § 431.196 before any compliance determination is made.
2. **Scope list.** Enumerate every part 431 section whose source note carried 89 FR 91163; the editorial note says "several sections," and Subpart K accounts for only § 431.192 and § 431.196 on the face of the current notes.
3. **Enactment date of Pub. L. 119-8.** Not stated in the source consulted and not material to the answer, since DOE effected the removal on Sept. 9, 2025; record it for the file.
4. **Appendix A edition.** Confirm no incorporation-by-reference edition in appendix A was tied to the disapproved rule; the current source note shows none.

## Practical consequence for Subpart K compliance work

For distribution transformers, the operative standards text on 2026-11-21 is the Dec. 22, 2024 version of § 431.196, read with the § 431.192 definitions as they stand after the Jan. 21, 2025 amendment (90 FR 6795). The § 431.193 test procedure and appendix A are unchanged by either action. Any internal compliance matrix keyed to the 89 FR 91163 standards must be retired and re-based on the Dec. 22, 2024 text, subject to closing verification item 1.
